### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via mcp.json (literal, a string literal in doorAuthor), mcpServers (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `42c4ceb2597f3840c382f2cc6785c35716ec99fb` — the merge of head `063eef161f308ecdec3aae00595acddcebc6ecee` into base `90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 42c4ceb2597f3840c382f2cc6785c35716ec99fb && git checkout 42c4ceb2597f3840c382f2cc6785c35716ec99fb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879 063eef161f308ecdec3aae00595acddcebc6ecee && git checkout -B drift-repro 90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879 && git merge --no-ff 063eef161f308ecdec3aae00595acddcebc6ecee

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 90f7555e426b29c871643fe58423869352cc0879` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The diff adds `EXTERNAL_DRIVER_CONTRACT_V2`, `EXTERNAL_DRIVER_CONTRACTS`, `ExternalContract`, `ExternalDoorInput`, optional `contract` on `ExternalInfoSchema`, optional `door` on `ExternalAuthorInput`, `ExternalDriver.contract` / `speaksDoor` / `assertDoor`, and `readDoorArm` / `DoorArmOptions`. The unreleased `_V1` alias is gone. Against cloud `main` `2da4757` `packages/service-ai-studio/src/evals/scenario-driver/contract.ts`: `_InfoFits` (:114) is unchanged; author and ask inputs widen `contract` to the `/1 | /2` union (`:128`, `:145`), which cloud's `/1` literal still satisfies; `door` is optional. By type reasoning cloud compiles and answers at the pin move (not run on a cloud pin tree).
- The wire stays backward compatible: the `info` input is always `/1` (`:285`); an answer with no `contract` reads `/1`; an unknown name is refused naming it; later inputs carry the answered name; a `/1` command is never handed a door (`assertDoor`, called at `cli.ts:578` before any card and again before any process).
- Token: only in a 0600 file in its own temp directory outside the call's cwd, removed in `finally`; the input carries `url` and `configFile` only; never on argv, env or stdin; the process record holds no argv or stdin. Pinned by `external-driver.test.ts` (fake command reports `keyOnArgv`/`keyInEnv`/`keyOnStdin` false) and `orchestrate.test.ts` (record, recording, scorecard and gallery export hold no token).

### ② Semver level

- `patch`, right. The level follows the `Metadata-protocol` kind; `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` ruling A). `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: this is a runner process contract, no authorable key moves. Both lines are line-initial in the changeset and the PR body, matching. The changeset sentence now states that `EXTERNAL_DRIVER_CONTRACT` keeps `/1` and names `_V2`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Round-1 should-fix resolved: `orchestrate.test.ts` adds a `runScenarios([... '--modes','door' ...])` rejection with a `/1` stand-in; it asserts the named refusal, empty `out`/`work`, and no turn sent. The dev's ablation (delete the `cli.ts` `assertDoor` call → red) is stated.
- Nit resolved: README says building through the door alone is the external command's to keep, since the runner cannot enforce it there.
- Accepted deviations: the two `cli.ts` door gates widened to `external:` (same defect class, in the fence); `--door-rules` refused for an external command naming why.
